clusters.evidence_quality_delta: Tight fight: both sides empirical with controlled experiments. Hybrid side has latency-controlled numbers (56x SetFit speed, within-2% hybrid); pure-LLM side has few-shot Banking77 wins but weaker cost reporting.
clusters.fight: Should intent classification use a small fine-tuned classifier (SetFit, optionally hybrid-routed to an LLM) or a native LLM few-shot classifier?
clusters.scope_overlap: Genuine disagreement under different operating constraints: accuracy-at-any-cost favors LLMs; latency/cost-constrained production favors SetFit+routing. The assignment needs both quality AND 15-minute reproducibility, which privileges the hybrid.

claims: SetFit + negative augmentation + MC-dropout uncertainty routing to LLM stays within ~2% of native-LLM F1 at ~50% less latency; SetFit alone is ~56x faster than the best LLM
Fine-tuning BERT/IntentBERT on ~1k labeled utterances beats heavier pre-training paradigms for few-shot intent; contrastive SetFit reaches near-full-data performance with 8 examples/class
Cost-aware Banking77 study: SetFit-class methods effective at 20 examples/class; LLM querying needs RAG-style cost reduction to be viable for budget-limited orgs
side_a.position: Small fine-tuned classifier first (SetFit/IntentBERT-style), LLM only on uncertain routes

claims: GPT-3.5/4 in-context learning outperforms fine-tuned non-generative models on Banking77 with even fewer examples; human-expert-selected examples beat random ones
LLM few-shot intent needs no gradient training and handles wording variance better than small encoders
side_b.position: Native LLM few-shot classifier outperforms fine-tuned small models

clusters.evidence_quality_delta: Tightest fight in the corpus: both sides have high-citation empirical work. Pro-judge side has correlation numbers up to .81 on narrow tasks; skeptic side has causal bias mechanisms plus cross-domain failures. Resolution is task-scoped, not global.
clusters.fight: Can an LLM judge be trusted as the reply-quality metric, or is human judgment irreplaceable?
clusters.scope_overlap: Both right in different scopes: on narrow, rubric-pinned tasks with mitigation + human-anchoring, judges approach human reliability; on open-ended, culturally-situated, near-perfect-output discrimination, they fail. The assignment is closer to the second scope, so the judge must be caged, not crowned.

claims: G-Eval with GPT-4 + CoT reaches Spearman .514 with humans on summarization/dialogue, beating prior reference-free metrics
Output-based LLM judges reach Pearson .81/.68 with humans on code translation/generation, near-human with balanced score distributions
Bias-calibrated longitudinal judge holds tau .59-.68 with weekly Bradley-Terry correction
side_a.position: LLM judges usable with rubric + mitigations + human anchoring

claims: Position bias flips ~35% of GPT-4 verdicts on order swap; verbosity and self-preference persist; swap-debiasing cannot remove self-enhancement bias (formal decomposition)
Best LLM judge human-equivalent on only 4/11 criteria in global-health eval; juries fix one more; Kinyarwanda inputs degrade cost-effectiveness
GEMBA-style judges correlate .09 with humans on near-perfect MT until rubric+span fixes lift to .35
side_b.position: LLM judges systematically biased; human agreement evidence mandatory, never assumed

clusters.evidence_quality_delta: Hybrid side has convergent production testimony (5+ independent engineering sources) plus a vendor measurement (Anthropic 35-67%); pure-dense side rests on benchmark-era generality and small-scale sufficiency arguments. Hybrid leads on evidence weight.
clusters.fight: Does the support agent need hybrid (BM25 + dense + fusion + cross-encoder rerank) retrieval, or is pure dense retrieval enough?
clusters.scope_overlap: Scoped by query mix: pure dense wins on paraphrase-heavy semantic matches; hybrid wins on exact identifiers (order numbers, handles, error codes), rare terms, and short noisy tweets. Twitter support traffic is identifier- and noise-heavy, favoring hybrid — but the margin must be measured, not assumed.

claims: Pure dense fails silently on exact identifiers, code, rare terms; BM25+dense RRF fusion with wide top-k then rerank is the production default
Contextual retrieval (chunk+context embeddings) cuts retrieval failures substantially when paired with reranking
Recommended baseline: index both BM25 and dense, default RRF, evaluate against pure-dense with ranking metrics
side_a.position: Hybrid + rerank beats either alone and is the default to beat

claims: At small scale a single embedded store with one good embedding model suffices; second retrieval path doubles ingest/ops cost for unmeasured gain
Dense-first with metadata filtering covers most paraphrase variance in short customer utterances
side_b.position: Pure dense suffices at this scale; hybrid is over-engineering until proven

clusters.evidence_quality_delta: Small-taxonomy side has the only controlled experiments varying label-space size/scope (intent-age paper); large-taxonomy side has benchmark-reuse convenience but documented close-intent confusion. Evidence favors small.
clusters.fight: Should the brand intent taxonomy be small and data-derived (5-10 intents) or large and preset (Banking77-style, dozens)?
clusters.scope_overlap: Both useful at different stages: Banking77 legitimate for prototyping intent methods (assignment explicitly allows intent-work-only use); the submission taxonomy itself must be small, derived from the brand, and OOS-robust.

claims: LLM OOS detection degrades with larger label spaces and broader intent scopes; fine-grained labels + smaller spaces are better for OOS
GPT-generated augmentation helps only when intents are sufficiently distinct; close intents get cross-contaminated generations
77-label schemes guarantee rare-intent starvation in a 150-250 golden set
Banking77 (13k/77 intents) is the standard few-shot intent benchmark with curated human-expert subsets and error analyses worth reusing for method validation
side_b.position: Reuse large preset taxonomy for intent work

clusters.evidence_quality_delta: No-framework side has convergent practitioner testimony (discussion + 3 engineering writeups); framework side has capability arguments but no measurement on this task shape. Minimum-complexity principle + evidence both point to plain pipeline unless agents prove a measured win.
clusters.fight: Should the agent be built on an agent framework (LangChain/LangGraph/LlamaIndex/PydanticAI) or as a plain Python pipeline with direct LLM calls?
clusters.scope_overlap: Scoped by task shape: multi-step tool-orchestration favors frameworks; single-shot classify-retrieve-generate-escalate favors plain code. This assignment is the second shape.

claims: LangChain no longer a requirement for simple RAG in 2025; plain Python + direct APIs + vector store is faster to build, debug, maintain
Engineers moving to native agent architectures; frameworks accelerated wave one, production demands control
Rebuild-without-LangChain reports concrete debuggability and latency wins
side_a.position: Plain pipeline; no agent framework unless it proves a measured win

claims: DSPy programs (not prompts) with optimization, LangSmith/Langfuse tracing+evals give systematic improvement loops frameworks provide out of box
side_b.position: Frameworks provide eval/observability/program structure worth the overhead

clusters.evidence_quality_delta: Comparisons agree on feature matrices; the decisive point (custom golden + agreement evidence is non-delegable) is argued, not measured — but follows directly from the assignment text.
clusters.fight: Should evaluation use a hosted/code-first suite (RAGAS/DeepEval/promptfoo/LangSmith) or a custom harness?
clusters.scope_overlap: Both: use suite components where they fit (promptfoo CI shape, RAGAS faithfulness probes as secondary signals) but the headline harness must be custom — no suite ships golden-set sampling docs, leakage guards, or judge-human agreement for this brand.

claims: promptfoo fits CI, DeepEval is code-first, RAGAS covers RAG metrics, LangSmith/Braintrust cover tracing — each fits a different stack; pick by stack
side_a.position: Adopt a suite as the harness

claims: All suites rely on the same biased LLM-judge mechanism — design around it rather than inheriting it blindly
RAGAS-style reference-free metrics need human-agreement validation per deployment; unvalidated suite scores prove nothing
side_b.position: Custom harness with suite parts as secondary signals only

clusters.evidence_quality_delta: Calibrator side shows 6-16% AURC gains in-domain; skeptic side shows no method consistently beats MaxProb across tasks AND settings (IID/OOD/ADV). Synthesis: MaxProb + held-out calibration + reported AURC is the defensible floor; learned modules must beat it to justify themselves.
clusters.fight: Should escalation use a calibrated confidence threshold (MaxProb + temperature scaling + held-out threshold) or a learned abstention module?
clusters.scope_overlap: Genuine methods disagreement resolvable by experiment: implement MaxProb+calibration first, report risk-coverage/AURC, and only keep a learned calibrator if it beats MaxProb on a temporal holdout.

claims: Calibrating with confidence + difficulty signals improves risk-coverage AUC 6-16% over MaxProb in IID and OOD
Temperature scaling cuts ECE ~31% without accuracy loss; entropy/margin separate correct from incorrect for selective prediction
Small toolkit computes risk-coverage, AURC/AUGRC, and picks thresholds from a calibration split — the production pattern
side_a.position: Calibrated thresholding over a tuned confidence signal

claims: Across 17 datasets × IID/OOD/ADV, no selective-prediction method consistently and considerably outperforms MaxProb; gains do not transfer across tasks
Unnecessary abstention has its own cost — selective-selective-prediction work shows naive thresholds over-abstain
side_b.position: MaxProb baseline is sufficient; fancy modules do not transfer

clusters.evidence_quality_delta: Light side has benchmark + comparison evidence at relevant scale; heavy side has production-ops arguments that only bind above this assignment's scale. Light wins for the submission; heavy noted as the scale-up path.
clusters.fight: Does the submission need managed/heavy storage (managed vector DB, Postgres+pgvector, Elasticsearch) or do embedded stores (FAISS/Chroma/LanceDB + SQLite/DuckDB) suffice?
clusters.scope_overlap: Scale-scoped: subsample eval (thousands of threads) runs in-process; full-3M indexing and multi-tenant serving would change the answer. Optimize for fast reproducible subsample, keep interfaces swappable.

claims: pgvector brings vector search into the production database; Elasticsearch unifies BM25+dense+learned-sparse behind one retriever interface
Managed services remove index-ops burden at team scale
Local-RAG benchmarking across Chroma/Qdrant/FAISS/pgvector shows embedded options competitive at small scale with far less setup
Polars+DuckDB outperform pandas 10-100x on multi-million-row ETL without distributed systems; reproducible benchmark harness exists across 7 engines
side_b.position: Embedded + file-backed stores suffice and reproduce fastest
